input.question: Why do chewing gums that have their main ingredient as sugar/corn syrup still include Aspartame in their recipe?
input.ground_truth: Here's a quotation from Wrigley on the subject: The Wrigley Company utilises the high intensity sweetener, Aspartame, in a number of its products - as the primary sweetener in some of our sugarfree brands and as a flavour enhancer in some of our sugar-sweetened brands. As an ingredient, Aspartame has the added benefit of providing an especially long-lasting flavour.

So, they put both sugar (or corn syrup) and Aspartame to make it taste super sweet for a long time.
